question: Should OpenClaw intentionally reject unsafe numeric byte-size config values during validation/runtime parsing instead of preserving the old rounded behavior for upgrades?
rationale: The code fix is narrow and correct, but repository policy treats stricter config validation as compatibility-sensitive because existing configs can start failing or lose the threshold behavior after upgrade.

options.title: Accept strict safe-integer byte sizes
options.body: Land the PR as the canonical boundary because unsafe JavaScript integers cannot represent the user-requested byte count exactly.

options.title: Add upgrade guidance first
options.body: Ask for a doctor/docs or warning path before merge if maintainers want existing unsafe numeric configs to get a clearer recovery path.

options.title: Preserve rounded numeric config
options.body: Keep current compatibility if maintainers decide rejecting these edge-case values is too disruptive for existing installations.

recommendation.title: Accept strict safe-integer byte sizes
recommendation.body: Land the PR as the canonical boundary because unsafe JavaScript integers cannot represent the user-requested byte count exactly.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a CLI/config byte-size parsing behavior, and this handle is both listed for CLI ownership and tied to the parser's feature history.
